measures.title: Proposal to Amend Utah Constitution - Publication Amendments (H.J.R. 10, 2025)
measures.summary: The Utah Constitution now requires proposed constitutional amendments to be published in a newspaper in each county for two months before the general election. Amendment A would instead require publication for 60 days immediately before the general election in a manner set by state law. If it passes, H.B. 481 (2025) would have the Lieutenant Governor post the full text on the Utah Public Notice Website and the Lieutenant Governor's website; legislative analysts estimate savings of up to $1.4 million every two years.
measures.yesMeans: Proposed amendments would be published for 60 days before the election as set by state law (online, under H.B. 481) instead of in newspapers. Takes effect January 1, 2027.
measures.noMeans: The Constitution keeps requiring proposed amendments to be published in newspapers in each county for two months before the election.

measures.title: Proposal to Amend Utah Constitution - Statewide Initiatives (S.J.R. 2, 2025)
measures.summary: Most citizen-proposed statewide initiatives in Utah pass with a simple majority. Amendment B would require at least 60% voter approval for initiatives voted on after November 1, 2026 that create a new tax, expand an existing tax, raise a tax rate, or change a property tax rate so it falls less than it would under existing law. It would not change the vote needed for other initiatives.
measures.yesMeans: Citizen initiatives that increase taxes compared to existing law would need at least 60% of the vote to pass. Takes effect November 23, 2026.
measures.noMeans: Citizen initiatives that increase taxes would continue to pass with a simple majority.
